key_insight: STReasoner teaches large language models to perform explicit spatio-temporal reasoning on time series by combining spatial-aware reinforcement learning with LLM reasoning, yielding more interpretable and causally grounded outputs than purely predictive models.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between predictive accuracy and explicit spatio-temporal reasoning in time-series problems (e.g., traffic, power grids, disease spread) where models must synthesize temporal dynamics, spatial dependencies, and textual context for high-stakes decisions.
method: Introduce spatial-aware reinforcement learning to fine-tune or guide LLM reasoning policies so they respect spatial structure and temporal dynamics.
Couple LLM chain-of-thought generation with graph-structured spatial priors and reward shaping that promotes correct etiological and spatio-temporal inferences.
Evaluate using ST-Bench, a focused benchmark of four core tasks (including etiological reasoning) designed to measure interpretability and causal/spatio-temporal reasoning beyond prediction.
impact: Makes LLMs practical for high-stakes time-series domains by improving their ability to explain and justify spatio-temporal inferences; enables more trustworthy decision support and diagnostic analysis in real-world systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM + spatial-aware RL loop with graph input, reward signals, and chain-of-thought outputs
Benchmark overview: grid showing the 4 ST-Bench tasks with short descriptions and example inputs/outputs
Case study map+timeline: spatial map (e.g., traffic network or infection spread) linked to a temporal sequence and model reasoning highlights
Performance comparison chart: accuracy/interpretability vs. standard baselines and ablations (with RL and without RL)
paper_title: STReasoner: Empowering LLMs for Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in Time Series via Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Juntong Ni, Shiyu Wang, Ming Jin, Qi He, Wei Jin
